name: NKT275
manufacturers: Newmarket Transistors (defunct; no primary datasheet located)
description: The germanium PNP used in the earliest Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face units (mid-1960s), famously associated with Jimi Hendrix's rig. Made by the UK's Newmarket Transistors, which stopped production by the early-mid 1970s; original examples are now rare and expensive collector items, commonly hundreds of dollars each, and are frequently counterfeited or relabeled given fuzz-pedal demand. Newmarket is long defunct with no successor maintaining documentation, so this entry is built from period catalog data rather than a manufacturer's own current datasheet -- see gotchas before relying on it.

typical_application: Historically a general-purpose germanium audio transistor; today almost exclusively sought for recreating or repairing early Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face circuits.
gotchas: PIN POSITION NOT VERIFIED: no primary manufacturer package drawing was found. Do not wire from this entry alone; test a real part's E/B/C with a multimeter diode-test (or a curve tracer) before building anything

no primary Newmarket datasheet is known to survive online; the electrical data here comes from a scanned period component catalog reached only through an aggregator mirror, cross-checked against one independent lookup source. Both agree on Vcbo/Vebo/Pd/Ic/hFE(min)/Tj but disagree on fT and Cob
genuine NOS NKT275 units are rare, valuable (commonly hundreds of dollars), and frequently counterfeited or relabeled; measure hFE and leakage on any purchased part before trusting the label
germanium: leakage current (ICBO) is far more temperature-sensitive than silicon; keep well below rated dissipation
